content.title: About
content.content: The McDonald's Cheeseburger is a classic fast‑food item featuring a beef patty, melted cheese, pickles, onions, mustard and ketchup, all sandwiched between a soft sesame‑seed bun. It first appeared on the menu in the 1960s and has become one of the chain’s most popular items.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first cheeseburger was served in the 1940s at the original McDonald’s restaurant in San Bernadino, California.
Portion sizes and exact ingredients may vary by country, but the core recipe stays the same.
In 2020 McDonald’s launched a limited‑edition “Cheeseburger Deluxe” with a double patty and extra cheese.
The sesame bun contains about 2 g of sesame seeds, adding a small amount of healthy fats.
The cheeseburger is often used as a “base” product in promotional combos and new menu experiments.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: The beef patty provides roughly 12 g of high‑quality protein, essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Red meat is rich in heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Melted cheese adds a modest amount of calcium, important for bone health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and bun supply B12, B6 and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: With about 300 kcal, the cheeseburger provides a fast source of energy, useful during high‑intensity activities.

items.title: High calories and saturated fat
items.content: One cheeseburger contains roughly 300 kcal and 12 g of saturated fat, so it should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Sauces and cheese can contribute over 600 mg of sodium, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The product contains milk, gluten, and may have trace soy, important for people with allergies.

items.title: Preservatives and additives
items.content: In some markets, the sauces may contain artificial flavors and preservatives.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cheeseburgers are typically eaten warm, holding the bottom bun. They pair well with fries and a drink, or can be crumbled into salads or other dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Consume the fresh burger immediately. If needed, store it in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours and reheat to 75 °C in a microwave or oven.
